questions.question: When driving at highway speeds, you should look ahead about ____ to spot problems early.
questions.explanation: Watch the road 12 to 15 seconds ahead. At highway speeds, this distance is about a quarter mile.

questions.question: When backing with a trailer, turning toward the driver's side is better because:

options.text: It gives the driver a better view.
Turning toward the passenger side is illegal.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gives the driver a better view.
questions.explanation: Back toward the driver's side. This way, you can see your path better as you back up.

questions.question: Stopping distance is affected by:
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on vehicle speed, weight, and road surface grip.

questions.question: Broken suspension parts are:
questions.explanation: The suspension holds up your vehicle and keeps the axles in place. Broken parts are very dangerous.

questions.question: To avoid hitting a hazard on the road:

options.text: Swerving may be safer than stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Swerving may be safer than stopping.
questions.explanation: Sometimes swerving is safer than stopping. You can usually turn away faster than you can stop completely.

questions.question: Power steering hoses should be checked for:

options.text: The right amount of brake fluid.

questions.explanation: Check power steering hoses, pumps, and fluid level. Look closely for any leaks.

questions.question: Texting while driving is very dangerous because:

options.text: It takes both your attention and one hand off the road.
People get too focused on their phones.

questions.correctAnswerText: It takes both your attention and one hand off the road.
questions.explanation: Texting is dangerous because it distracts your mind and requires you to remove your hands from the steering wheel.

questions.question: You should check your mirrors:
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors regularly to see traffic around you and spot any problems with your vehicle.

questions.question: If your vehicle is hydroplaning, you should:
questions.explanation: Do not brake if your vehicle hydroplanes. Instead, take your foot off the accelerator and push in the clutch to slow down.

questions.question: When turning, you should:

options.text: Turn off your signal just before turning.
Signal only if other cars are ahead.

questions.explanation: Use your turn signal well before you turn or change lanes. Keep it on during the turn. Turn it off after the turn is done.

questions.question: Can you use radial and bias-ply tires together?

options.text: Yes, they can be used together.
Yes, they can be used together on the front of the vehicle.
No, they should not be used together.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, they should not be used together.
questions.explanation: Do not use radial and bias-ply tires together. All tires on your vehicle should be the same type and size.

questions.question: When should a driver use turn signals when changing lanes?

options.text: Always use turn signals when changing lanes.
Only use turn signals if another vehicle is next to you.
Do not use turn signals if the lane change is obvious.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use turn signals when changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning or changing lanes. This tells other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.question: Why should you check your tires regularly in very hot weather?

options.text: Heat can cause tire air pressure to increase.
The tread wears down faster in hot weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Heat can cause tire air pressure to increase.
questions.explanation: Air pressure inside tires increases when the temperature is hot. Pay close attention to tire pressure and mounting when driving in hot weather.

questions.question: When checking windshield wiper blades, what condition should they be in?
questions.explanation: Check wiper blades for damage, stiff rubber, and to make sure they are firmly attached to the vehicle.

questions.question: When using a fire extinguisher, what should you do?

options.text: Stay as far away as possible from the flames.
Use any extinguisher on any type of fire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay as far away as possible from the flames.
questions.explanation: Stay away from the fire and aim at the base of the flames, not the top. Different fires need different treatments. If you are unsure, wait for trained firefighters.

questions.question: If you must drive through flowing water or a large puddle, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Avoid driving through water if possible. If you must drive through it, slow down and gently apply the brakes. This keeps water and mud out of the brake system.

questions.question: Is it important to know what is happening behind your vehicle while driving?
questions.explanation: You need to know what is happening around your entire vehicle at all times. Use your mirrors often to stay aware of your surroundings.

questions.question: Where is the tire load information printed?

options.text: On the side of the tire.
On the inside of the tire.
On the inside of the driver's door.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the side of the tire.
questions.explanation: The tire load, or maximum safe weight a tire can carry, is printed on the side of each tire.

questions.question: How should a lane change be made?
questions.explanation: Lane changes should be made slowly and smoothly.

questions.question: During a pre-trip inspection, which of the following should you NOT check for?

options.text: Tires with too much air pressure.

questions.explanation: When checking tires, look for proper tread depth, wear, and air pressure. Check that all tires are the same size. The manufacturer does not matter as long as the tires match in size and type.
